nodes.description: Public string state variable holding the current question, written by set_game and NewQuestion.
Address state variable acting as the game owner/admin; gates StopGame, NewQuestion and newQuestioner.
bytes32 state variable storing the hash of the expected answer; read by Try and written by set_game/NewQuestion.
External payable function that verifies the response hash, requires msg.sender == tx.origin and msg.value > 3 ether, then transfers the whole balance.
Payable initializer that sets responseHash, question and questionSender only when responseHash is unset.
Payable function restricted to questionSender that transfers the entire contract balance out.
Payable function allowing questionSender to overwrite question and responseHash.
Function allowing questionSender to transfer ownership of the game to a new address.
Payable fallback function accepting ether with no logic.
Caller address used for authentication, ownership assignment and as the recipient of fund transfers.
Transaction origin used in Try's require(msg.sender == tx.origin) check, providing only weak anti-contract protection.
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) inside Try, an external value transfer sending the full contract balance to the caller.
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) inside StopGame, an external value transfer draining the contract balance to questionSender.
String answer supplied by the caller, hashed with keccak256 and compared against responseHash.
Question text supplied by the caller and stored in the question state variable.
Answer supplied by the caller, hashed and stored as responseHash during initialization.
New question text supplied by questionSender and written to the question state variable.
New answer hash supplied by questionSender and written to responseHash.
Address supplied by questionSender to become the new questionSender/owner.

edges.reason: msg.sender is compared with tx.origin in Try's require, so the caller controls whether execution proceeds to the payout.
tx.origin is read inside Try's require and used as the only anti-contract guard, a weak authorization dependency.
When the guess and msg.value conditions hold, Try executes the full-balance transfer unsafe operation.
The transfer recipient is msg.sender, so caller-controlled data flows directly into the external value transfer.
StopGame executes the balance transfer unsafe operation once the owner check passes.
StopGame sends the whole balance to msg.sender, an externally controlled recipient.
StopGame requires msg.sender == questionSender, so the caller identity gates the function body.
questionSender state variable is read in StopGame's ownership check.
NewQuestion only performs its writes when msg.sender == questionSender.
questionSender state variable gates the state changes performed by NewQuestion.
newQuestioner only changes ownership when msg.sender == questionSender.
questionSender is compared against the caller before transferring ownership.
The newAddress parameter is written into questionSender, transferring privileged ownership.
set_game writes the keccak256 hash of the response into responseHash.
set_game stores the supplied question text into the question state variable.
set_game assigns msg.sender as the initial questionSender.
msg.sender becomes questionSender inside set_game when responseHash is unset.
Try reads responseHash to compare it against the hashed answer.
The _response parameter is hashed and compared inside Try, driving the payout condition.
NewQuestion overwrites responseHash with the owner-supplied hash.
NewQuestion overwrites the question state variable.
The _question parameter of set_game flows into the question state variable.
The _response parameter of set_game is hashed into responseHash.
The _question parameter of NewQuestion is written to the question state variable.
The _responseHash parameter of NewQuestion is written to responseHash.
msg.sender triggers the payable fallback function, depositing ether into the contract.

normalization_plan.reason: The _response parameter only exists to feed the hash comparison inside the Try function.
The _question parameter is a temporary input consumed by set_game when storing the question.
The _response parameter is a temporary input consumed by set_game when computing responseHash.
The _question parameter is a temporary input consumed by NewQuestion when updating the question.
The _responseHash parameter is a temporary input consumed by NewQuestion when updating responseHash.
The newAddress parameter is a temporary input consumed by newQuestioner to reassign ownership.
